sections.name: Shine
sections.lead: Finishes that move under light. The tool draws a flat plate; watch.js holds grain, weave and brush patterns for the watch, none for the dial. The Finishes section's groove rule says how each would be drawn under one sun.

sections.name: Lume at night
sections.lead: Night shots. The whole watch becomes one glowing graphic: bezel, chapter ring, hands. This is the Day · Night switch in Next, and the notice when hands and markers glow differently.

sections.name: Cases, lugs and bracelets
sections.lead: Four cases in CASES, all round (field cushion 1939, diver SPB143, Emre's prototype, dress Calatrava); two bracelets on lugs, closed round a wrist since 4.94.18. No square, TV, tonneau or integrated case.

sections.name: Leather and straps
sections.lead: Leather in three tones per colour with a pore-and-crease grain; NATO in six stripe sets with a weave; buckle, keepers, taper. No stitch line, no suede nap, no rubber.

sections.name: Dial preparation
sections.lead: The makers' side: enamel on the firing mesh, stone blanks, a one-page spec sheet, a CAD render used as a brief. The proof-sheet idea, seen from where it is needed.

sections.name: Type and clock faces
sections.lead: Clocks and watches where the type is the dial. Seventy-five open fonts in the tool, one per ring, upright or on the path; Michroma and Audiowide for the Eurostile look, Arimo for Helvetica's metrics. No word numerals, no numerals turned to the radius, no disc dial.

sections.name: Lettering and classics
sections.lead: How dial lettering is drawn, classic dials with their own numeral logic, and a cloisonné enamel at three stages. Text rings exist; hand lettering, a Breguet set and two colours in one ring do not.
